question: Can a TD-error-seeking exploration rule that detects and caps persistently high-TD-error transitions reach the sparse-reward goal faster than the plain TD-error-seeking rule in a small stochastic-reward gridworld?
method: Tabular Q-learning with error-seeking action selection on a simulated gridworld (sparse goal, noisy costly cells). Learning runs over agent seeds; main score is mean environment steps to first goal on held-out evaluation seeds.

dataset.name: Simulated stochastic-reward gridworld (generated in code)
dataset.source_url: none: generated in code, no download

metric_name: mean environment steps to first goal on held-out evaluation seeds (lower is better; capped at the step budget)
baseline: Tabular Q-learning; actions chosen by argmax of running mean |TD error| per state-action pair (stand-in for SEE's error-seeking objective), eps=0.05.
improved: Same agent, but each state-action pair keeps a TD-error history; pairs whose |TD error| stays high without decaying are flagged stuck and their exploration value is capped at the median visited value.
notes: Simulated toy environment; tabular Q-learning, not SAC with neural networks, so this is only a stand-in for SEE. Hyperparameters were fixed a priori and not tuned, so no cross-validation selection was needed; the held-out evaluation seeds were used once for the final scores. Steps are censored at the step budget. Only three agent seeds; no significance test. The stuck detector thresholds are design choices and results may not favour the improved variant.
